prior.title: No fresh question after the moment
prior.expected: After the fix, Ben asks a new question so he can answer better alone.

prior.expected: After the coaching moment, a fresh question lets him retry 'the dog is wet' on his own.
prior.got: Only 'Back to the conversation'; the next question is unrelated and the session ends at the next turn.
evidence: #5 'Back to the conversation'; #6 'What did he do next?'; #11 '0 on your own · 1 moment to keep'.

prior.title: No replay with a fresh question after the moment
prior.expected: After the 'small' moment, a new question lets him try the coached word alone.
prior.got: Only 'Back to the conversation'; next question is about having a dog.
evidence: #9 'Back to the conversation'; #10 'Thank you! Do you have a dog?'; #11 still Czech

prior.expected: One tiny sentence and one simple question with known words.
evidence: #12 'Rex is a nice name! Is Rex a large dog?'; #15 'Is he the same size as Biscuit?'; #16 'fast and strong'

prior.title: Situation list long and mixed
prior.got: 20 entries incl. booking, lost jacket, group project.

prior.title: No fresh question after the moment
prior.expected: After the coaching moment a fresh question lets him retry 'likes' alone.
prior.got: Back to the conversation goes to an unrelated question and the mission ends.
evidence: #16 'Back to the conversation'; #17 'Where does he sleep at night?' with 'Mission done'.

prior.title: Cue is generic and repeated
prior.expected: Cue he can say to the question, e.g. 'My dog is big.'
prior.got: 'Try: My dog is ... He likes to ...' for size and for likes.

evidence: facts evidence last quote 'My dog like sleep' supported:false; #18 '2 on your own'.

prior.title: Grammar note too abstract and fix changes sentence
prior.got: 'With one dog, add s to like' and model 'likes to sleep' while he said 'like sleep'.

criteria.evidence: No placement in this journey; level set by hand to A1.
#7 recognition task: 'Which sentence tells what you build?' with two short options, under 15 words.
No line made him feel he failed; #11 'Good: you told Leo what you like.'
#1 list has 20 situations incl. 'A booking that is missing', 'Our group project', 'The lost jacket', school-like and travel items, unsuited to a nine-year-old who wants play.
#9 'Creepers are cool! Do you build a house in Minecraft?' two short sentences, one question, known words.
#11 'with an s, the usual way to say it' is abstract for a 9-year-old; also the note drops 'Dog.' and the fix 'I like dogs' changes what he said.

done.evidence: #2-#10 Help me answer, Choose a phrase and Pause & coach found in-scene; #11 coach screen reached without leaving Leo's conversation.

#8 he typed 'I like creeper. Dog.' after the phrase choice, not the offered phrase; the help (#3 'I build a ___') did not shape the reply. #11 note quotes 'I like creeper.' and omits 'Dog.', so not what he really said.
#11 offered 'Replay the moment' but he pressed finish at #11; no fresh question and no better answer shown, #12 ended.
#12 '0 on your own · 1 with help'; evidence marks supported:true for both quotes.

judgeAgreement.disagreements: No placement tasks in this journey.

findings.title: Replay with fresh question never exercised
findings.expected: After coaching, a fresh question lets him retry alone.
findings.got: Finished at coach screen; no retry and no better answer shown.
findings.evidence: #11 'Replay the moment' / 'Finish for today'; he chose finish; #12 '0 on your own'.
findings.suggested_acceptance: After coaching, the replay offers a new question and the retry is recorded as independent if unsupported.

findings.title: Coaching note abstract and drops what he said
findings.expected: Tiny child wording quoting 'I like creeper. Dog.'
findings.got: 'with an s, the usual way to say it'; the quote omits 'Dog.'
findings.evidence: #11 'You said I like creeper.' vs #8 'I like creeper. Dog.'
findings.suggested_acceptance: Note quotes the whole reply and uses child words, e.g. 'one creeper, many creepers'.

findings.title: Cue generic and help loop repeated
findings.expected: Cue that moves him on; Help pressed once is enough.
findings.got: Help pressed 4 times with the same 'Try: I build a ___. It is ___.'
findings.suggested_acceptance: Repeat press escalates to a new kind of help (phrase choice) at once.

findings.title: Situation list long and mixed
findings.got: 20 entries incl. booking, lost jacket, group project.
findings.suggested_acceptance: Elementary profile shows only play, animal, sport situations.

findings.title: Partner turns tiny and on topic
findings.got: 'Creepers are cool! Do you build a house in Minecraft?' and a simpler version.

judge.voice: Leo was fun, Minecraft! I liked the question about creepers. But I pressed help four times and got the same "I build a ___" every time, which was boring. Then I typed my own thing anyway. The coach said something about "an s", and I didn't understand that. It also forgot I said "Dog". I wanted to try again with a new question, but I just finished. It said I did it with help, so I think that's fair. Would I use it again? Maybe, for Minecraft. The long list of situations with jackets and bookings looks like school. Mum would like that it didn't make me feel bad.

prior.evidence: #11 Replay offered but not taken; fresh question never shown.
#9 'Creepers are cool! Do you build a house in Minecraft?' stays simple.
#1 list of 20 incl. 'A booking that is missing', 'The lost jacket'.
#3-#6 identical 'Try: I build a ___. It is ___.'
#12 '0 on your own · 1 with help' with Czech-free supported replies marked supported.
#11 'with an s, the usual way to say it' and fix adds 'I like dogs'.

verdictWhy.text: D2 failed: #8 he typed 'I like creeper. Dog.' after the phrase choice, not the offered phrase; the help (#3 'I build a ___') did not shape the reply. #11 note quotes 'I like creeper.' and omits 'Dog.', so not what he really said.
verdictWhy.check: The help actually unblocks the next reply; a coaching note quotes what they really said.

verdictWhy.text: D3 failed: #11 offered 'Replay the moment' but he pressed finish at #11; no fresh question and no better answer shown, #12 ended.
verdictWhy.check: Replaying the moment gives them a fresh question, and they answer it better than before.

verdictWhy.text: C4 failed: #1 list has 20 situations incl. 'A booking that is missing', 'Our group project', 'The lost jacket', school-like and travel items, unsuited to a nine-year-old who wants play.
C6 failed: #11 'with an s, the usual way to say it' is abstract for a 9-year-old; also the note drops 'Dog.' and the fix 'I like dogs' changes what he said.
